title: Connor Hellebuyck to join list of Olympic legends awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom
content:
President Donald Trump announced Tuesday in his State of the Union address that Team USA men’s hockey goalie Connor Hellebuyck would be awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor, in light of Hellebuyck’s heroics in Sunday’s gold medal game against Canada.

“I’ve never seen a goaltender play as well as goalie Connor Hellebuyck,” Trump said, with 17 of the 25 members of the team in attendance.

The medal is traditionally awarded to individuals to recognize a lifetime of significant achievements in the arts, public service, science or other fields. Hellebuyck anchored Team USA’s 2-1 overtime win over Canada, saving a record 41 of the 42 shots he faced and spearheading the United States’ first men’s hockey gold in 46 years.

“We’re going to be talking about this performance for generations,” U.S. winger Brady Tkachuk said after the win. “It was an all-time performance from a superstar at his position. It’s going to go down as one of the best performances of all time.”

The performance earned Hellebuyck inclusion on an exclusive list of U.S. Olympians to be awarded the honor. While 19 athletes, coaches and sports figures who have competed in the Olympics have been awarded a Medal of Freedom, only a few have received it primarily for their Olympic performances. Other gold medal winners like Muhammad Ali, Dan Gable, Michael Jordan, Jim Thorpe and Babe Didrikson Zaharias were awarded the medal at least in part because of the broader successes of their athletic careers.

Here are the individuals who earned the nation’s most prestigious award for their Olympic and international sporting significance.

The Black sprinter defied Nazi Germany and Aryan supremacy ideologies at the 1936 Berlin Games by winning gold in the 100m, 200m, long jump and 4x100m relay. Owens was the most successful of five Black athletes on the U.S. men’s track and field team that year, who combined to earn eight gold medals. He was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1976 by President Gerald Ford, four years before Owens died.

Biles is the most decorated American gymnast ever, with 32 Olympic and World Championship medals. Her seven Olympic golds are the most by an American gymnast.

In 2021, she testified in Congress about failures in the investigation of widespread sexual abuse by former USA Gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar. Biles has also advocated for children in the foster care system, as she was a former foster child. President Joe Biden awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2022, making Biles the youngest person to receive the award.

Rapinoe was a key star of the U.S. women’s national soccer team during a dominant period in the squad’s history. She won two FIFA Women’s World Cups (2015, 2019), a gold medal at the 2012 London Games and a bronze medal at the 2021 Tokyo Games. Rapinoe’s 73 goals with the USWNT are tied for the third most in program history.

Biden awarded her the Medal of Freedom in 2022, partly for her successful fight for equal pay for women’s athletes and for helping to make U.S. Soccer the first federation to equalize pay for men’s and women’s teams.

Ledecky is the only female swimmer to win an individual event at four consecutive Olympics. In total, she is a nine-time Olympic gold medalist and has won 14 medals across four Olympics from 2012 to 2024, and has broken 17 world records in her career.

Biden awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2024 for being “a humble leader, Olympian and champion of unparalleled determination.”

Correction: A previous version of this article misstated the number of players from the U.S. men’s Olympic hockey team present for the State of the Union address. Although 20 made the trip to Washington, D.C., 17 were seen at the speech.
